portrait.headline: You keep moving into another country's music, and somehow you ended up back in Tokyo.

observations.claim: You move into one language at a time and stay a couple of years.
observations.evidence: Everything you liked in 2020 was Korean. Everything in 2018 was English. Then in 2022 it was Taiwanese bands and Cheer Chen, with almost nothing else.

observations.claim: You go to the old masters first, then find who's doing it now.
observations.evidence: Chet Baker and Bill Evans came first, and Laufey followed a few months later. Before that, D'Angelo and Erykah Badu came a year ahead of Daniel Caesar.

observations.claim: Four songs from anyone is your limit, and then you're gone.
observations.evidence: Eight artists got exactly four songs each, including Frank Ocean, IU and Fujii Kaze. Nobody ever got a fifth.

observations.claim: You came back to Japanese music, but this time to people releasing records now.
observations.evidence: Your first likes were Anri and Tatsuro Yamashita, songs that were already decades old. Ten years later you're liking Gen Hoshino and Fujii Kaze.

observations.claim: In every language you end up with a man singing falsetto.
observations.evidence: It's Frank Ocean in English, Zion.T in Korean and Khalil Fong in Mandarin. Each one showed up in a different year.

eras.label: Back in Japan
eras.text: First you picked up the city pop revival bands, then Gen Hoshino and Fujii Kaze got you liking songs with a bit of bounce.

eras.label: Old jazz, then new
eras.text: You started with Chet Baker's hushed standards and moved on to Laufey and some soft English dream pop.

eras.label: Quiet piano
eras.text: Solo piano and indie folk took over, with Ryuichi Sakamoto and Nujabes keeping the volume low.

eras.label: Chinese-language years
eras.text: You liked Cantonese ballads from Eason Chan, then Mandarin R&B, then the Taiwanese indie scene.

eras.label: Seoul
eras.text: Nearly everything was Korean and current, from DEAN's late-night R&B to IU and the indie bands.

eras.label: Records from before your time
eras.text: You liked 80s Tokyo city pop, then Brazilian bossa nova, then 90s neo-soul like D'Angelo, almost all of it decades old.
